name: Prolifasin
description: Prolifasin is a recombinant growth factor complex that dramatically accelerates tissue regeneration in damaged organic structures, combining targeted angiogenic stimulation with controlled stem cell mobilization. Originally developed for trauma surgery, it has become the standard of care for any procedure involving augment installation, removal, or revision. A full-dose Prolifasin course can reduce healing time for major surgical trauma from months to weeks.
effects: accelerated cellular regeneration at wound and surgical sites
enhanced vascular regrowth to augment-adjacent tissue
reduction of necrotic tissue at implant edges
stimulation of nerve regrowth in damaged peripheral pathways
overall faster return to pre-injury baseline
side_effects: elevated metabolic demand — patients must consume significantly more calories
low-grade fever during active regeneration phases
rare: uncontrolled proliferation (benign tumorous masses) at injection site
can accelerate growth of pre-existing undiagnosed malignancies
joint and bone aches as regeneration prioritizes soft tissue
psychological restlessness — users describe feeling 'too alive'
cultural_context: Prolifasin is the drug that makes the augmentation lifestyle viable — without it, the physical trauma of chrome installation would require months of recovery. Tier 2-3 users budget for Prolifasin as part of augment costs. On the Gray Zone, black-market Prolifasin equivalents are dangerous: often under-dosed, impure, or missing key growth factor components, leading to partial healing and chronic complications. Prolifasin is also used off-label by bodymod enthusiasts who heal from extreme modifications at accelerated rates. The 'too alive' feeling of active regeneration has a cult following.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone street surgeon has gotten hold of a massive quantity of expired Prolifasin — it still works, but the degraded growth factors are causing unpredictable tissue responses in patients, some miraculous, some deeply wrong.
Someone is using Prolifasin to keep a critically injured person alive long enough to extract information — the body is healing faster than it can be damaged, creating a horrifying interrogation loop.

Helix Biosystems has discovered that Prolifasin interacts with a specific geneware modification to produce a spontaneous regenerative effect far beyond anything in the drug's design — and has been secretly identifying and monitoring users who have this combination.
